title: Maximum Number of Ones
statement: You fill a grid `M` that has `width` columns and `height` rows with zeros and ones. The filling is allowed only if every square block of `sideLength` by `sideLength` adjacent cells inside the grid holds at most `maxOnes` ones. Return the largest number of ones an allowed grid can contain.
signature: int maximumNumberOfOnes(int width, int height, int sideLength, int maxOnes)
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every grid is hopeless, so look at what the rule really constrains. Label each grid cell by its position inside a `sideLength` by `sideLength` tile, `(row % sideLength, col % sideLength)`. Every square block of that size contains each label exactly once. So if we pick at most `maxOnes` labels and put a one on every cell carrying one of them, every block holds at most `maxOnes` ones, and the grid is allowed. An optimal grid can always be built this way, so the only question is which labels to pick. Labels near the top-left corner of the tile repeat more often across the grid than those near its far edges, so the greedy choice is the `maxOnes` labels with the most copies.

## Approach

1. For each label `(row, col)`, count its copies: `rowCopies` grid rows and `colCopies` grid columns carry it, so it appears `rowCopies * colCopies` times.
2. Store these products in `counts` and sort them from largest to smallest.
3. Add up the first `maxOnes` of them into `ones` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`width = height = 3`, `sideLength = 2`, `maxOnes = 1`. Label `(0, 0)` appears in rows 0 and 2 and columns 0 and 2, so 4 times; `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` appear 2 times each; `(1, 1)` only once. Sorted `counts` is `[4, 2, 2, 1]`, and taking one entry gives `4`: ones in the four corners.

## Complexity

- Time: O(s² log s) for `s = sideLength`: s² labels are counted and sorted.
- Space: O(s²) for `counts`.

## Pitfalls

- A label `p` along a side of length `n` appears `floor((n - p - 1) / sideLength) + 1` times, not `n / sideLength`; the leftover strip at the edge matters.
- Width counts columns and height counts rows; mixing them up only works on square grids.
- `maxOnes` can be 0, in which case the answer is 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `counts` | how many grid cells carry each label |
| `row`, `col` | a label: a position inside the tile |
| `rowCopies`, `colCopies` | grid rows and columns with that label |
| `ones` | total ones placed so far |
| `i` | index into the sorted `counts` |
